candidates.original_title: The relation between perception and behavior, or how to win a game of Trivial Pursuit
candidates.description: Priming participants with intelligence-related professor concepts causes better performance on a general-knowledge trivia task than priming them with stupidity-related soccer-hooligan concepts.
candidates.citation_sentence: Although Dijksterhuis and van Knippenberg (1998) initially found evidence for overall effects of priming condition on trivia performance, the replications conducted by Dijksterhuis, van Knippenberg, and Holland produced a smaller overall effect of priming condition (a 2%-3% difference) and showed moderation of this effect by gender: Men showed a difference (9.3% and 7.6%), but women did not (0.3% and -0.3%).
candidates.notes: The paper reports a meta-analytic aggregate of 23 qualifying direct replications across laboratories. The original reference does not provide a DOI.
